A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, methods, experiments and theoretical analysis. The complete main texts and Appendices A and B are readable, allowing reliable comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training experiments on parity, single-index models, in-context linear regression and modular addition, including intervention and ablation results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The data-repetition and multiphase procedures, MLP and Transformer models, and initialization, learning-rate and normalization interventions are unchanged. The added appendix paragraph about µP restates an existing comparison.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same sparse and dense parity tasks, Hermite single-index models, in-context linear regression and modular addition. No additional dataset, domain or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same large-set/online, repeated-subset, multiphase, µP and α-scaling comparisons. The new appendix Figure 15 duplicates Figure 7 and introduces no comparator.

E3.justification: The setup and Appendix B.1 retain the same metrics, model configurations, batch sizes, test-set sizes, hyperparameter sweeps and training schedules. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The random-label, input-bias, initialization, layerwise learning-rate, width/depth, scheduling and QK-normalization analyses are retained. The additional µP paragraph and duplicate figure redisplay existing evidence rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging performance over random seeds and report 256 seeds for Figure 5. The plotted uncertainty bands are unchanged, with no added run-count disclosures or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All unique plotted panels are identical across versions, and the numerical findings in the text are retained. Figure 7's revised caption explicitly states that µP fails to close the SIM gap, but this finding was already reported in v1's accompanying text and appendix.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and the assumptions, lemmas and proofs in Appendix A retain their mathematical content. The update equations are displayed and numbered differently, without changing the updates or convergence bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central claims: smaller repeated datasets can accelerate learning, sampling biases adjust relative layer growth, and suitable parameter interventions can reduce the small-vs-large gap.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanation and limitations concerning nonconvex learning, real-world language corpora, architecture dependence and QK normalization are unchanged. The added µP summary repeats the existing parity-versus-SIM qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 retains the same architecture specifications, initialization details, optimizer settings, data schedules and hardware information, including the A100/four-hour description for Figure 5. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against prior explanations are unchanged. Related work becomes Section 2, and the added µP paragraph repeats existing citations. Removing the Johnson–Zhang bibliography URL does not remove the cited work.

P1.justification: Related work is promoted from subsection 1.1 to Section 2, and two prior-theory subheadings become paragraph headings. v2 adds an acknowledgment to Depen Morwani and a short µP recap. Most prose is retained; one formerly valid section reference becomes '??' on page 8.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography and reflows text, equations and figures while retaining the panel designs. Figure 7 receives a clearer task-specific caption, and its identical plots are repeated as appendix Figure 15, renumbering subsequent figures.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence, proofs and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Figure 7's clearer caption offers a small presentation benefit, but duplicate Figure 15 retains the older overbroad caption, and v2 introduces a broken section reference on page 8. These limited editorial gains and defects do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
